content_voiceover: This slide visually reinforces the distinction between reactive thrombocytosis, essential thrombocythemia, and prefibrotic myelofibrosis using bone marrow histology and lab correlates. Reactive thrombocytosis shows a relatively normal appearing marrow without clonal megakaryocyte changes. Essential thrombocythemia typically presents without anemia, with normal red cell indices including MCV and RDW, no leukoerythroblastosis or dacrocytosis on the peripheral smear, a usually normal LDH, and a JAK2 mutant allele burden generally under twenty percent. Prefibrotic myelofibrosis, in contrast, often shows anemia with abnormal red cell indices, increased RDW and decreased MCV, may show leukoerythroblastosis and dacrocytes, teardrop cells, on the peripheral smear, an elevated LDH, and a JAK2 allele burden that can exceed twenty percent. These clinical and laboratory clues matter because outcomes diverge significantly, ET has an excellent ten year survival of eighty nine percent with low rates of leukemic transformation, zero point seven percent, and progression to myelofibrosis, zero point eight percent. Prefibrotic myelofibrosis has a lower ten year survival of seventy six percent, and substantially higher rates of leukemic transformation at five point eight percent and progression to overt myelofibrosis at twelve point three percent. So recognizing prefibrotic MF matters for prognosis and counseling, not just for pathology reports.
keypoints: ET usually lacks anemia, has normal red cell indices, and no leukoerythroblastosis
Pre-PMF often has anemia, abnormal RDW and MCV, and possible teardrop cells or leukoerythroblastosis
JAK2 allele burden tends to stay under twenty percent in ET, may exceed twenty percent in pre-PMF
Ten year survival is eighty nine percent in ET versus seventy six percent in pre-PMF
Leukemic transformation and myelofibrosis progression are markedly higher in pre-PMF
keypoint_voiceover: Beyond marrow morphology, simple peripheral clues separate these entities, anemia, abnormal red cell indices, teardrop cells, elevated LDH, and higher JAK2 allele burden all point toward prefibrotic myelofibrosis rather than true ET. This distinction carries real prognostic weight, since pre-PMF has meaningfully worse survival and higher transformation risk.
